follow_up_notes: Do not update docs/wiki from this watch artifact directly; run the normal raw-source ingest workflow if these updates should be synthesized.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Google Cloud MCP documentation now describes IAM-based access control for Google and Google Cloud remote MCP servers, including project-level and resource-level control, project tags, read-only or read-write tool use, the Tool User role, and the mcp.tools.call permission.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: When this raw source is ingested, keep broad Google Cloud MCP background upstream and retain only the local control pattern: resource-scoped MCP authorization, least-privilege roles, and read/write capability separation.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: Local MCP practice pages should keep treating tool access as an identity and authorization design problem, not only a server configuration detail.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: TechRadar reports that enterprise AI agents need first-class identities, named owners, defined purposes, scoped permissions, creation/review/expiry lifecycle records, and audit trails preserving both the initiating human and executing agent.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Ingest should focus on owner, identity, lifecycle, and audit roster practices; route general security ecosystem detail upstream.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: This reinforces local practice leaves around tool governance, adoption agreements, ownership rosters, and human approval boundaries.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: The article frames human approval as an enforceable control-plane pattern: agents propose actions, a deterministic policy/enforcement point evaluates evidence, approvals capture exact payloads and scope, and execution is allowed only when the approved and executed payloads match.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Future wiki synthesis should emphasize approval packages, exact-payload matching, policy-as-configuration, and audit evidence rather than chat-only confirmation.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: This is directly relevant to local approval-boundary and tool-call governance leaves because it separates prompt behavior from deterministic authority enforcement.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Business Insider sponsored content from Dell AI Factory with NVIDIA says agentic workflows can consume far more tokens than chatbots, making tokenomics a P&L issue; it argues for cost-per-outcome thinking and selectively running workhorse agent workloads locally for governance, privacy, and predictable infrastructure economics.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Keep vendor/product details upstream; local synthesis should capture workload-routing criteria, token-cost telemetry, and cost-per-outcome framing.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: This updates local operating-model and infrastructure-economics leaves with current public language around cost visibility, local/cloud routing, and cost-per-outcome metrics.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: VS Code documentation describes custom instruction categories, AGENTS.md support, file-scoped .instructions.md files, organization-level instructions, instruction priority, generation commands, diagnostics, and the deprecation of settings-based code/test generation instructions in favor of file-based instructions.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Ingest should keep product mechanics minimal and update local guidance on instruction layer precedence, file boundaries, diagnostics, and durable project-owned rules.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: This is a current public source for durable instruction-file practice and the separation between always-on repository guidance, scoped instruction files, and user or organization-level rules.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: LeafWiki describes a Markdown-on-disk wiki model with tree navigation, full-text search, revision history, link refactoring, backup/restore, and public or private modes; the Jul 25 v0.12.0 entry highlights backup and restore, two-factor authentication, drag and drop, favorites, and editor resizing.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Route product specifics upstream if needed; local pages may use it as evidence that durable wiki workflows benefit from portable Markdown files, link maintenance, and recovery features.
qualifying_updates.visible_date_basis: Home page Latest from the blog lists Jul 25, 2026 LeafWiki v0.12.0.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: The update is relevant as public evidence for lifespan-organized documentation, clipping/raw-intake portability, and leaf-watch assumptions about folder-oriented Markdown knowledge bases.
